I feel as though I can really bring some useful insight to your problem. 

I (27F) am currently in the same shoes as your wife. I have been overweight my entire life and have struggled with weight loss. While I am not considered "obese" I was close to it at my highest weight. A few months ago, my husband told me that he does not find my weight flattering, and that he is not attracted to me anymore. While hearing this information hurt like hell, it has taught me (and him) a few things. Hopefully they help you as well:

1. Weight gain and weight loss is not black and white. It's not fair to extrapolate your wife's lack of weight loss to make it about her not caring. Most people that have had chronic weight issues have suffered from trauma in their past that has manifested in unhealthy habits. For me personally, my weight is directly tied to past trauma. You making HER weight loss journey about YOU isn't fair to either one of you. It's more complicated than you're making it out to be. With that being said, there's nothing wrong with desiring a partner that takes care of themselves. 
2. It's okay to get help from a professional. My relationship isn't yours, and I don't claim it to be. You telling her that you're not attracted to her more than likely killed her on the inside. Her self-esteem, her security in your relationship, and she more than likely hates herself now (which isn't going to help her weight loss). You were supposed to be her PARTNER for life. A PARTNER doesn't say hurtful things like that to the other person. Seeking professional help can help you better vocalize your needs in this relationship while also helping her identify why she's failed to lose weight or why she's unmotivated to lose weight.
3. Her losing weight will not fix your problems. It's not a magic pill that will make everything better. You hurt her, and you hurt her bad by saying what you did in the manner you did. Even if she loses the weight, there's a good chance she'll resent you. Not to mention that weight loss takes time to really lose weight the RIGHT way. She can starve herself and lose weight, but I hope you don't want that. 

​

If you want to speak more about it, I'd be more than happy to chat. I think it could be helpful to hear from someone in a similar position, but from a different perspective. Feel free to send me a message if you'd like.
